# Tone and Style

## Sincerity

> status: ratified (D-0025)

True fantasy with allegory undertones — genuine and authentic, never arch or ironic.
No winking, no meta, no modern quips. The characters' world is real to them; its
terrors and beauties are treated with full weight.

## Adult register

> status: ratified (D-0082)

Dark enough to be pitched at adults; never immature, stagey anime writing aimed at
teens. Real wisdom and perspective in the narrator; plausibility in the characters.
Subtext over announcement: people talk about rations, weather, and repairs, and mean
love, fear, and defiance. Songs, poetry, and scraps of ancient history weave in
naturally; dialogue sounds utterly real and human. The whole serves a pro-humanistic
narrative that is, in the end, a new flavor of fantasy adventure.

## The allegory discipline

> status: ratified (D-0004, D-0030, D-0046)

Literal elements stay truly pre-modern; the technology allegory is a tool, never
foregrounded; everything must be fully readable/hearable as pure hard-magic fantasy.
Operationally: the banned-vocabulary list (`data/banned-vocabulary.yaml`) is enforced
on all diegetic text — "machine" was the precedent rejection.

## What we never do

> status: rejected (D-0076)

No trauma-drama exploitation — the Walking Dead / Outlander mode of awful things
happening and happening (especially to women) as engine or spectacle. Related dead
registers, rejected elsewhere and listed here for writers' convenience: shouty shōnen
posturing (D-0065, D-0066), monster-of-the-week grind (D-0012), Freytag quest
escalation (D-0052), musical magic (D-0002), foregrounded tech vocabulary (D-0046).

## Dialogue doctrine

> status: provisional (D-0083)

The working models: Gilroy's Andor (terse, transactional, working-class; rebellion in
subtext) and Mantel's Wolf Hall (politeness as leverage); Portis for the apprentice's
exact, stubborn formality; Le Guin/Clarke for the narrator's mythic dryness. Nobody
monologues a backstory; nobody narrates their feelings. The protagonist's register,
once pending here, is since ruled — see [[protagonist]] and §The register map below.

## Voice silhouettes and the indirectness guard

> status: ratified (D-0163)

Speaking styles (and eventually accents) work like the at-a-glance silhouettes of
anime character design: every party and faction is distinguishable by ear within a
line or two. The narrator's remove, the koans, and the found artifacts carry the
elevated flavor; Enfys sounds strange — and the people around her REACT to the
strangeness. The guarded failure mode is the zen-textbook exchange: when Enfys and
Aalto both go oblique, the scene reads as manner, not character. Aalto is the
viewpoint and never too weird to us — provincial, inexperienced, young — and asks
the plain question the listener would ask. The full register map, an open question
(Q-0019) when this section landed, is since ruled — see §The register map below.

Diction has a geography (D-0165): each region's speech patterns, syntax leanings,
and word-stock mirror its naming register — the Welsh-flavored hedge country, the
Norse-flavored crags, the Latinate stratum of the keeps — with occasional loan
words as texture. There are no true invented languages in this world, ever; the
strangeness lives in pattern and preference, never in a conlang.

## The register map

> status: ratified (D-0166, D-0168, D-0176, D-0179)

The silhouette map is ruled (record: docs/rulings/RQ-020-tone-register-map.md). The
narrator reads as the Reading-Scholar — elevation lives in the koan cold-opens and
outros only, with at most one future-knowledge tell an episode. D-0176 tightens this:
the narrator must remain largely invisible, third-person, and largely omniscient
through future artifacts such as histories, woven records, songs, and quoted
scholarship. Narration may not address the audience directly, announce the tale's
promise, or sell the scene's function. Enfys is the Courteous-Guest: full-grammar
courtesy over iron, contractions vanishing under Archive strain, at most two oblique
beats a scene and every one reacted to within two lines; her surfacing minds arrive
as clear register events in their own regional silhouettes. Aalto is the
Counting-Voice: evidence before conclusion, real questions. Geir speaks late,
verdict delayed. Folk speech splits logistics from threshold blessing-forms; the
keeps speak two strata of doublespeak (the Benevolent Ledger officer over the Tally
Clerk). Turning readings walk their argument; artifacts keep their own palette.
Dialect is idiom and rhythm on the page — accents belong to casting; eye-dialect
never. Darkness plays austere-with-warmth; humor is dry, embedded, and generated by
register collision itself, never quips.

D-0168 confirms the campaign-006 darkness result as permission, not a dial change:
wounds and damage may carry promise structure and take real on-mic time, but only
inside the austere-with-warmth and no-exploitation line already ruled here.

D-0179 clarifies the audio surface: the project is closer to an audiobook with
cast and foley than an old-school radio play. SFX and foley support orientation and
texture, but they do not carry precise meaning as a major character. The narrator
is allowed and required to do windowpane work where audio-only action would
otherwise demand unrealistic listener inference.

## No male gaze

> status: ratified (D-0023, D-0024)

Inherited from the author's own Frieren/Inuyasha analyses: dignified, practical
character presentation; no fan-service framing; female characters' worth never tied
to attractiveness or to men; psychological sovereignty throughout.
